## What this tutorial does

This document shows how to estimate an *optimum level or critical value* under model uncertainty using:

\- multiple candidate response models,

\- bootstrap aggregation (bagging) by fitting a randomly selected candidate model to each bootstrap resample and pooling the resulting optimum estimates.

The dataset and the specific optimum definition used here are only examples. The workflow is the main deliverable.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Setup

```{r}
# Core packages
library(tidyverse)
library(minpack.lm)   # nlsLM

# Data I/O
library(readxl)

```

# Data

## Load dataset

```{r}
dat <- read_excel("./case_study_AONR.xlsx", sheet = "Trial_27") |>
  dplyr::select(
    input_level = Total_N_SI,
    response    = Yield_SY
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(input_level), is.finite(response))

if (!nrow(dat) || length(unique(dat$input_level)) < 3L) {
  stop("Trial_27 requires at least three distinct finite nitrogen rates.")
}
```

## Visual check

```{r}
ggplot(dat, aes(input_level, response)) +
  geom_point() 

```

# Bagging (random model per resample)

The bagging workflow is adapted from the bootstrap aggregation approach developed by Francisco Palmero for EONR estimation ([original implementation](https://github.com/FranciscoPalmero/Bagging_EONR_estimation)). This tutorial uses the AONR response models and fitting rules of the accompanying case study.

## Define candidate response functions

```{r}
# Linear Plateau Model
lin_p <- function(x, a, b, xs){
  if_else(x < xs,
          a + (b*x),
          a + (b*xs))
}

# Quadratic Plateau Model
quad_p <- function(x, b0, b1, b2){
  xp  <- b1/(2*b2)
  x_2 <- x^2
  xp_2 <- xp^2

  if_else(x < xp,
          b0 + (b1*x) - (b2*x_2),
          b0 + (b1*xp) - (b2*xp_2))
}

# Mitscherlich Model
mits <- function(x, b0, b1, b2){
  b0 + (b1 - b0) * exp(-b2*x)
}

```

## Fit candidate models to the original data

The bootstrap fits use the full-data coefficients as starting values, as in the original case study.

```{r}
linear_start <- coef(lm(response ~ input_level, data = dat))

fm.LP <- nlsLM(response ~ ifelse(input_level < xs,
  a + b * input_level, a + b * xs),
  data = dat,
  start = list(
    a = unname(linear_start[1]),
    b = unname(linear_start[2]),
    xs = unname(quantile(dat$input_level, 0.6, na.rm = TRUE))
  ),
  control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 1024)
)

fm.QP <- nlsLM(response ~ ifelse(input_level < b1 / (2 * b2),
  b0 + b1 * input_level - b2 * input_level^2,
  b0 + b1 * (b1 / (2 * b2)) - b2 * (b1 / (2 * b2))^2),
  data = dat,
  start = list(
    b0 = unname(linear_start[1]),
    b1 = unname(linear_start[2]),
    b2 = unname(abs(linear_start[2]) /
      (2 * quantile(dat$input_level, 0.6, na.rm = TRUE) + 1e-8))
  ),
  lower = c(b0 = -Inf, b1 = -Inf, b2 = 1e-10),
  control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 1024)
)

fm.MIT <- nlsLM(response ~ b0 + (b1 - b0) * exp(-b2 * input_level),
  data = dat,
  start = list(
    b0 = unname(max(dat$response, na.rm = TRUE)),
    b1 = unname(min(dat$response, na.rm = TRUE)),
    b2 = 1 / unname(max(dat$input_level, na.rm = TRUE))
  ),
  lower = c(b0 = -Inf, b1 = -Inf, b2 = 1e-10),
  control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 1024)
)

LP_start <- as.list(coef(fm.LP))
QP_start <- as.list(coef(fm.QP))
MIT_start <- as.list(coef(fm.MIT))
bounds <- range(dat$input_level)
```

## Bagging procedure

Generate all bootstrap samples first, then select one of the four response models for each sample. This order preserves the random draws in the original case study.

```{r}
set.seed(123)
K <- 5000L
n <- nrow(dat)
model_choices <- c("LP", "QP", "MIT", "QUA")

bootstrap_rows <- replicate(K, sample.int(n, n, replace = TRUE))
bag_model <- sample(model_choices, size = K, replace = TRUE)
```

## Fit random models to each bootstrap resample

Only the selected model is fitted for each sample. Failed fits are recorded as missing estimates and excluded from the summary.

```{r}
bagg_models <- vector("list", K)

for (i in seq_len(K)) {
  db <- dat[bootstrap_rows[, i], , drop = FALSE]
  mtofit <- bag_model[i]

  fitM <- try(
    switch(mtofit,
      LP = nlsLM(response ~ ifelse(input_level < xs,
        a + b * input_level, a + b * xs),
        data = db, start = LP_start,
        control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 1024)),
      QP = nlsLM(response ~ ifelse(input_level < b1 / (2 * b2),
        b0 + b1 * input_level - b2 * input_level^2,
        b0 + b1 * (b1 / (2 * b2)) - b2 * (b1 / (2 * b2))^2),
        data = db, start = QP_start,
        lower = c(b0 = -Inf, b1 = -Inf, b2 = 1e-10),
        control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 1024)),
      MIT = nlsLM(response ~ b0 + (b1 - b0) * exp(-b2 * input_level),
        data = db, start = MIT_start,
        lower = c(b0 = -Inf, b1 = -Inf, b2 = 1e-10),
        control = nls.lm.control(maxiter = 1024)),
      QUA = lm(response ~ input_level + I(input_level^2), data = db)
    ),
    silent = TRUE
  )

  theta <- NA_real_
  par1 <- par2 <- par3 <- NA_real_

  if (!inherits(fitM, "try-error") &&
      (inherits(fitM, "lm") || isTRUE(fitM$convInfo$isConv))) {
    cf <- coef(fitM)

    if (mtofit == "LP") {
      theta <- unname(cf[["xs"]])
    } else if (mtofit == "QP") {
      if (all(is.finite(cf[c("b1", "b2")])) && cf[["b2"]] > 0)
        theta <- unname(cf[["b1"]] / (2 * cf[["b2"]]))
    } else if (mtofit == "MIT") {
      b0 <- cf[["b0"]]; b1 <- cf[["b1"]]; b2 <- cf[["b2"]]
      if (all(is.finite(c(b0, b1, b2))) &&
          b0 > 0 && b2 > 0 && b0 > b1)
        theta <- -log(0.05 * b0 / (b0 - b1)) / b2
    } else {
      # Centered quadratic optimum, matching the original case study
      xbar <- mean(db$input_level)
      xc <- db$input_level - xbar
      fit_centered <- try(lm(db$response ~ xc + I(xc^2)), silent = TRUE)

      if (!inherits(fit_centered, "try-error")) {
        qc <- coef(fit_centered)
        b1 <- unname(qc[["xc"]])
        b2 <- unname(qc[["I(xc^2)"]])

        if (all(is.finite(c(b1, b2))) && abs(b2) >= 1e-10) {
          theta <- -b1 / (2 * b2) + xbar
          if (b2 > 0) {
            pred <- predict(fit_centered,
              newdata = data.frame(xc = bounds - xbar))
            theta <- bounds[which.max(pred)]
          }
        }
      }
    }

    # Retain model coefficients for the tutorial's final figure
    if (all(is.finite(cf))) {
      par1 <- unname(cf[1])
      par2 <- unname(cf[2])
      par3 <- unname(cf[3])
    }
  }

  # Apply observed-range restriction after deriving the optimum
  if (is.finite(theta)) {
    theta <- min(max(theta, bounds[1]), bounds[2])
  } else {
    theta <- NA_real_
  }

  bagg_models[[i]] <- tibble(
    model = mtofit, par1 = par1, par2 = par2,
    par3 = par3, theta = theta
  )
}

df_bagg <- dplyr::bind_rows(bagg_models)
```

## Bagging results

```{r}
## Summaries by model (median + 95% CI)
theta_by_model <- df_bagg %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(theta)) %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    n       = dplyr::n(),
    estimate = median(theta, na.rm = TRUE),
    CI_2.5   = unname(quantile(theta, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE)),
    CI_97.5  = unname(quantile(theta, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups  = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::arrange(factor(model, levels = c("LP","QP","MIT","QUA")))

theta_by_model

## Overall Bagging estimate (median + 95% CI)
theta_bag     <- df_bagg$theta
theta_bag_hat <- median(theta_bag, na.rm = TRUE)
theta_bag_ci  <- quantile(theta_bag, c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

theta_bag_hat
theta_bag_ci

# Observed selection proportions (each model has probability 0.25)
prop.table(table(factor(bag_model, levels = model_choices)))

```

# Visualization

## Bagging bootstrap distribution

```{r}
ci <- quantile(theta_bag, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

theta_ci <- theta_bag[theta_bag >= ci[1] & theta_bag <= ci[2]]

hist(theta_ci,
     breaks = 30,
     main   = "Bagging bootstrap distribution (95% CI)",
     xlab   = "Bagging theta estimate")

```

## Model-specific bootstrap distributions

```{r, warning=FALSE}
theta_hist <- df_bagg %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(theta)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = theta)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 40, color = "black", fill = "gray80") +
  facet_wrap(~ model, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 350),
    breaks = seq(0, 350, 50)
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Estimate theta",
    y = "Frequency"
  )

theta_hist

```

## Final figure (data + candidate fits + Bagging)

```{r , fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
new.input_levels <- tibble(input_level = 0:320)

pars_hat <- df_bagg %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(theta)) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(model) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    par1_hat = median(par1, na.rm = TRUE),
    par2_hat = median(par2, na.rm = TRUE),
    par3_hat = median(par3, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pred_grid <- new.input_levels %>%
  tidyr::crossing(model = c("LP","QP","MIT","QUA")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pars_hat, by = "model") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    y = dplyr::case_when(
      model == "LP"  ~ lin_p(input_level, a = par1_hat, b = par2_hat, xs = par3_hat),
      model == "QP"  ~ quad_p(input_level, b0 = par1_hat, b1 = par2_hat, b2 = par3_hat),
      model == "MIT" ~ mits(input_level, b0 = par1_hat, b1 = par2_hat, b2 = par3_hat),
      model == "QUA" ~ (par1_hat + par2_hat*input_level + par3_hat*(input_level^2)),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

opt_points_bag <- theta_by_model %>%
  dplyr::select(model, x_opt = estimate, CI_2.5, CI_97.5) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(pars_hat, by = "model") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    y_opt = dplyr::case_when(
      model == "LP"  ~ lin_p(x_opt, a = par1_hat, b = par2_hat, xs = par3_hat),
      model == "QP"  ~ quad_p(x_opt, b0 = par1_hat, b1 = par2_hat, b2 = par3_hat),
      model == "MIT" ~ mits(x_opt, b0 = par1_hat, b1 = par2_hat, b2 = par3_hat),
      model == "QUA" ~ (par1_hat + par2_hat*x_opt + par3_hat*(x_opt^2)),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

Fig_bagging <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = dat, aes(input_level, response),
             alpha = 0.8, size = 1.5) +

  geom_line(
    data = pred_grid,
    aes(x = input_level, y = y, linetype = model)
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = opt_points_bag,
    aes(x = x_opt, y = y_opt, shape = model),
    size = 2.5, fill = "gray", stroke = 1.1
  ) +

  geom_point(aes(x = theta_bag_hat, y = 3000, color = "Bagging"), size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(y = 3000, xmin = theta_bag_ci[1], xmax = theta_bag_ci[2], color = "Bagging"),
                width = 0) +

  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 350), breaks = seq(0, 350, 50)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 14000), breaks = seq(0, 14000, 2000)) +

  scale_shape_manual(values = c(LP = 21, QP = 22, MIT = 24, QUA = 23)) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(LP = "solid",
                                   QP = "dotted",
                                   MIT = "longdash",
                                   QUA = "dotdash")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Bagging" = "black")) +

  theme_bw() +
  theme(panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
  labs(
    x = expression(Nitrogen~rate~(kg~ha^-1)),
    y = expression(Grain~yield~(kg~ha^-1)),
    linetype = "Response model",
    shape    = "Response model",
    color    = "Averaging method"
  )

Fig_bagging

```
